newsitem.title: UK: Industry oil stocks up 1.2 mln bpd in May - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Industry oil stocks up 1.2 mln bpd in May - IEA.

text.p: Oil stocks held by industry in the countries of the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) rose by 1.2 million barrels per day (bpd) in May but from significantly downward revised April levels, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.

The April revision from an estimated build of 0.8 million bpd to a draw of 0.5 million bpd was the largest monthly revision in the last several years, said the Paris based agency in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report.
A majority of the May rise occurred in product stocks which increased by 0.74 million bpd led by a 0.59 million bpd seasonal build in middle distillate inventories.
Gasoline and other oil products also rose (by 60,000 bpd and 170,000 bpd respectively) with most of the gains in the United States.
The very large downward revision in April helps explain the unexpected price strength during that month, the IEA said.
With April revisions the May stock change leaves total OECD stocks 25 million barrels below May 1995 (a period of normal stock levels) at 2,440 million barrels.

This was almost identical to the level that had been initially estimated for April 1997. Compared with May 1996 inventories are up by 72 million barrels, with North America 55 million above year earlier levels and OECD Pacific 23 million higher.
Due to April revisions however European stocks are only six million barrels greater than May 1996 stock levels.
About half (36 million barrels) of the year-on-year rise was in middle distillate stocks.
In the United States gains have been driven by a combination of very high refinery runs and product imports, especially of gasoline.
Despite strong economic growth and favourable pricing, stocks of products in the U.S. rose by 845,000 bpd during May, with about half being distillates.

In Europe rising German stocks in May were offset by falls in the Netherlands, Italy and Scandinavia. Most of the 200,000 bpd German stock build was in middle distillate (145,000 bpd) with gasoline and crude each up 35,000 to 40,000 bpd.

In the Pacific region, Japanese crude oil stocks rose in May by an estimated 191,000 bpd while other products and gasoline fell by 90,000 bpd and 27,000 bpd respectively, leaving overall inventory levels up 78,000 bpd over April and 19.7 million barrels above the May 1996 level.
